title: Slow Starters: Early-Season Patience and Buy-Low Targets
brief: Which players are likely to start the season slowly (rookies, players after long playoff runs, injury returns) and could be bought low in November trades? It must say how long to hold such players and which ones have early-season value instead.
summary: Three groups tend to start slowly: top rookies, players coming off a long Finals run, and players returning from injury. Target them in November trades when their owners are frustrated, and hold them at least two months, because their value comes in the second half and our fantasy playoffs (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28). Cheap early-season starters like Podziemski, Lendeborg, Reed and Isaiah Jackson are for October and November only. Plan to sell or drop each one before the injured starter ahead of him returns.

paragraphs.text: The notes point to three groups. The first is top rookies. They usually shoot poorly for about two months and then improve in the second half of the season. The second is players coming off a long Finals or championship run. Fatigue cuts their production, and their teams often rest them and trim their minutes early in the season. The third is players coming back from injury, who usually face a ramp-up, rest days and minutes limits.

In our player pool, Boozer, Peterson, Mikel Brown Jr. and Burries are the rookie cases. Brunson is the Finals-fatigue case, and he is also recovering from wrist surgery. Haliburton (Achilles), Ingram (partially torn Achilles), Coby White (calf), Konan Niederhauser and Duren (conditioning after a holdout) are the health or ramp-up cases. Jaylen Brown and VanVleet are slow for role reasons. Brown has to fit into a new team, and VanVleet's minutes are expected to rise only later.

The general rule is to trade for the long term. Buy low, sell high, and accept some short-term pain in the weekly matchups for a stronger roster in the March playoffs. In November, look for owners who are frustrated by poor box scores and managed minutes. The player's role should still be intact. Before you offer, check his minutes in games that are not back-to-backs. Those show the real role better than his season averages do.

Boozer is the best fit for this plan. Experts see him outside the top 70 early but at a top 25 to 35 level by February, March and the playoffs. Memphis also has a full 4-4-4 playoff schedule. If you missed him in the draft, offer for him in November or December, while his early numbers look like those of a player outside the top 70. Check his minutes in Iisalo's short-stint rotation and his three-point rate.

Haliburton's assists are elite and he has no weak category, and the notes expect him to be near his best by the fantasy playoffs. If his owner paid Yahoo's price and sees managed minutes and a rusty FG%, he is a fair buy-low target. Keep the offer near his round 2 value. His 3-4-3 playoff schedule is light, so the late ramp-up helps less in our format. Watch how Carlisle handles back-to-backs before Thanksgiving.

Jaylen Brown and Duren are softer buy-low targets. Philadelphia expects growing pains with Brown in October and November. Check his usage and whether his minutes reach 36. Duren may be eased in after missing preseason. Check whether his minutes get above 28 or stay near 27 while Paul Reed takes extra time. Brunson is different. His category value is mostly points, assists and FT%, and the Knicks' playoff schedule for a March 28 end is weak. Even after a slow start, do not pay the price of a 30 USD player for him.

If you drafted a top rookie, expect the slow start and do not drop him. Give him at least the first two months, which means through about mid-December, before you judge him. For Mikel Brown Jr., the notes say to wait until around February. He is outside our 144-player pool, so treat him as a waiver add in January, not as an early roster spot. Peterson is a 1 to 3 USD flyer whose FG% and turnovers should improve. Drop him only if he loses his starting minutes, not because of ugly October shooting.

Use our 4 IL slots for injury returns. Ingram is expected back between Thanksgiving and Christmas, with minutes limits after that. He is a cheap stash with a good 4-3-4 playoff schedule. Konan Niederhauser is out until about Christmas and is expected to start by February and March. Hold him only as a 1 USD final pick in an IL slot, or watch him on waivers. Coby White will likely miss the opening games. Hold him until he returns, then check whether he gets 30 or more minutes.

VanVleet's minutes are expected to climb from about 30 toward 34 or 35 later in the season, so do not drop him in November over a modest line. His 10-game playoff schedule is weak, though, so he is a sell or swap candidate before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline. Burries has no early path to minutes. He is a waiver name to track for a possible youth push near our March playoffs.

The notes split on how long a Finals hangover lasts. One side calls it a slow start: production dips and fatigue early, while teams cut starters' minutes at the start of the season. On that view, Brunson is a November buy-low who recovers. The other side says players slow down for the whole year after a long title run and are unlikely to repeat their production. On that view, a cheap November price is not a bargain. To decide, track Brunson's minutes and rest days. If his minutes return to normal by December while his production stays down, the full-season view looks right and you should not buy.

sections.heading: Early-season value: use it, then sell

paragraphs.text: Some cheap players have value only while a teammate is out. Podziemski and Lendeborg get bigger roles while Butler (and Moody, for Lendeborg) are out, and the Warriors are expected to fade later. Check in the first weeks that they start and play enough minutes. Plan to sell or replace them before Butler returns.

The same logic applies at center and on the wing. Reed's value depends on how fast Duren ramps up. Isaiah Jackson's starting job likely lasts until Konan Niederhauser returns around Christmas. Gafford may start while Lively, Johnson and Dharma are hurt. Grayson Allen starts while Knueppel and White are out. Derrick Jones Jr. starts while Ingram and Beal are out, but he is a short-term waiver pickup, not a draft pick. Each of these players is a 1 USD pick or a waiver add. Drop him as soon as the starter ahead of him returns. Keep our limit of 6 acquisitions per week in mind when you rotate them.
